sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Pati Tiwari,Deepak Upadhyay,Rajesh Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mukesh Kumar Pandey Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for informant as well as learned A.G.A for the State and perused the record 2.

This bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant-accused in case crime No.185 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Bidhuna, District Aurraiyya, with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is father-in-law of deceased.
The marriage of deceased with son of applicant has taken place about two years prior to the incident.
The allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased levelled against the applicant,are wholly false.

sentences.text: allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against all the accused persons, including the applicant.
It was submitted that the deceased has committed suicide by consuming some poison due to minor domestic dispute.
In post mortem report, except minor contusion, no injury has been shown on body of deceased and cause of death could not be ascertained, hence viscera was preserved.
As per FSL report, organo chloro insecticide has been found in the viscera of the deceased.

Statement of independent witness Lal Singh was referred, who has inter alia stated that marriage of deceased with son of applicant has taken place in a simple way and for some time deceased and her husband lived in Delhi and they have returned back to village only about one and a half months prior to the incident.

The said witness has further stated that only some hot talk took place between the applicant and deceased on account of some agricultural work and the husband of deceased has taken side of the applicant, due to which, deceased was annoyed and later on, her dead body was found in the pond behind the house of applicant.
Learned counsel submitted that deceased has committed suicide merely due to some domestic issue.

Lastly it has been submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 18.5.2023, having no criminal history,
and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
4. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for informant have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is father-in-law deceased.
It was submitted that deceased was being harassed on account of dowry and in fact, she was murdered by accused persons and after that, her body was thrown in the pond.
Statement of said witness Lal Singh was referred, wherein, said witness has also stated that some dispute has taken place between the deceased and applicant.

5. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Amar Singh involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate any of the prosecution witness.
iii. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the Amar Singh vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46655406/
2 evidence.
7.
